A NOTE ON THE NUMBERS

Read the evidence.
Then read the number.

What do ARR and annualized revenue mean?

ARR describes the annual recurring value of a revenue base. Annualized revenue projects a shorter period over a year and may include usage-based sales. We preserve the metric identified by each source. Neither is the same as audited full-year revenue.

Where do these figures come from?

“Company disclosed” means a company announcement. “Reported” means editorial reporting, sometimes citing a founder or an unnamed source. “Estimated” means a third-party research estimate. These labels describe provenance, not an audit or guarantee. Click any source to inspect it.

How current and comparable are the numbers?

This is a manually reviewed October 4, 2026 snapshot of selected observations, not a live feed or a complete market census. The “As of” column is the metric’s observation month where available; notes identify disclosure dates when the exact measurement date is unknown. Accounting, scope, and definitions differ. We do not sum the rows or calculate market share.

How are verticals assigned?

Verticals are Visionary Talks editorial categories based on the company’s principal product. A company can span several markets; this index assigns one primary category to make it easier to browse. Subsidiary figures refer to that business, not its parent group.
